people.name: Robert Sapolsky, PhD
people.key_contribution: Landmark research on cortisol/glucocorticoids and brain damage; 'Why Zebras Don't Get Ulcers' (popular science masterwork); HPA axis research; social hierarchy and cortisol in baboons
notable_works: Stress, Glucocorticoids, and Damage to Nervous System (1996)

people.name: Bruce McEwen, PhD
people.key_contribution: Coined 'allostatic load' concept; research on glucocorticoid effects on hippocampal plasticity; stress and brain adaptation; stress and metabolic syndrome connections
notable_works: The End of Stress As We Know It (2002)
Multiple publications on hippocampal plasticity and cortisol

people.name: Elissa Epel, PhD
people.key_contribution: PNAS 2004 landmark paper showing caregiver stress shortens telomeres by ~10 years equivalent; research on psychological stress and cellular aging; collaborated with Elizabeth Blackburn (Nobel)
notable_works: Epel ES et al. PNAS 2004 — Accelerated Telomere Shortening

people.name: Sheldon Cohen, PhD
people.key_contribution: Carnegie Mellon cold studies: experimental evidence that psychological stress increases rhinovirus susceptibility 3x; Social stress and immune function; PSS (Perceived Stress Scale) developer
notable_works: Cohen S et al. NEJM 1991 — Psychological Stress and Common Cold
PSS (Perceived Stress Scale) — most used stress measurement tool

people.name: Kelly McGonigal, PhD
people.key_contribution: Research on stress mindset: people who believe stress is enhancing vs harmful show different mortality outcomes; 'The Upside of Stress' (2015); TED Talk on stress and mortality
notable_works: TED Talk — How to make stress your friend (44M+ views)

people.name: Jon Kabat-Zinn, PhD
people.key_contribution: Founded MBSR (1979); pioneered secular mindfulness for chronic pain and stress; made mindfulness mainstream in medicine; basis for hundreds of RCTs

people.name: Sara Lazar, PhD
people.key_contribution: 2005 study showing meditators had thicker PFC (insular cortex + sensory cortices) than controls; first MRI evidence meditation changes brain structure
notable_works: Lazar SW et al. NeuroReport 2005 — Meditation experience is associated with increased cortical thickness

molecules.name: Cortisol
molecules.role_in_domain: Primary HPA axis output; acute survival; chronic elevation → hippocampal atrophy, visceral fat, immune suppression, insulin resistance

molecules.name: CRH (Corticotropin-Releasing Hormone)
molecules.role_in_domain: Hypothalamic trigger for HPA cascade; also anxiety mediator in amygdala; target of adaptogen modulation

molecules.name: DHEA-S (Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulfate)
molecules.role_in_domain: Counter-regulatory to cortisol; cortisol:DHEA-S ratio = allostatic load biomarker; declines with age

molecules.name: Adrenaline (Epinephrine)
molecules.role_in_domain: SNS acute stress response; immediate fight-or-flight; from adrenal medulla; faster than HPA cortisol

molecules.name: GABA (Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid)
molecules.role_in_domain: Primary anxiety inhibitor in CNS; depleted by chronic stress; supported by Mg, L-theanine, ashwagandha withanolides; target of benzodiazepines

molecules.name: IL-6 (Interleukin-6)
molecules.role_in_domain: Elevated in chronic stress; allostatic load biomarker; neuroinflammation mediator via BBB; correlates with depression and anxiety

molecules.name: Withanolides
molecules.role_in_domain: Active compounds in Ashwagandha; GABA-A allosteric modulator; anti-inflammatory; cortisol modulation via NF-κB pathway

molecules.name: HRV (Heart Rate Variability)
molecules.role_in_domain: Indirect measure of vagal tone / autonomic balance; low HRV = stress/sympathetic dominant; improved by slow breathing, mindfulness, exercise

organizations.name: Carnegie Mellon Stress & Health Lab
organizations.role: Sheldon Cohen's lab; definitive human stress-immunity challenge studies

organizations.name: UCSF Aging, Metabolism, and Emotions (AME) Center
organizations.role: Elissa Epel's center; telomere-stress research; meditation and aging

organizations.name: Osher Center for Integrative Medicine (UCSF/Harvard)
organizations.role: Mindfulness, meditation, and stress research; MBSR clinical translations

organizations.name: American Institute of Stress
organizations.role: Stress education and research dissemination; resources for health professionals

case_studies.title: Epel 2004 PNAS — Caregiver Telomere Shortening
case_studies.description: Mothers caring for chronically ill children showed telomeres equivalent to 10 years of accelerated aging vs control mothers; telomere length correlated with perceived stress level; landmark in psychoneuroimmunology connecting stress to cellular aging

case_studies.title: Cohen 1991 NEJM — Cold Susceptibility and Stress
case_studies.description: Participants exposed to rhinovirus; those with high perceived stress (PSS) were 3x more likely to develop clinical cold; dose-response: higher stress = higher susceptibility; controlled quarantine design (gold standard); foundational PNI evidence

case_studies.title: Goyal 2014 JAMA — MBSR Meta-Analysis
case_studies.description: 47 RCTs, n=3,515 subjects; moderate evidence for anxiety (d=0.38), depression (d=0.30), and pain; low evidence for stress/distress; mindfulness programs comparable to antidepressants for mild-moderate depression; no serious adverse events
